title: Nothing sweeter than love (III.5)
hook: love is swift, sincere, patient, brave
tomorrow: can losing the argument actually bring you peace?

segments.voice: Yesterday, book three opened on a quiet voice under the café noise. The line was speaking within. Today that inner voice starts to sing.

Ten at night. A kitchen. Someone's mom gets off the phone and says it plainly: your grandmother's having surgery next week, visit after, when she's settled. The girl at the counter already has the car keys in her hand. Her thumb is on the group chat, half a message typed: should i just go now? Is that too much? She's standing there, keys in one hand, phone in the other, and the cursor is blinking.
screen: `TEN AT NIGHT, KEYS IN HAND.` → `VISIT AFTER, WHEN SHE'S SETTLED.` → `SHOULD I JUST GO NOW?`

segments.voice: The Imitation of Christ has a chapter for that blinking cursor. Book three is mostly a quiet talk between Christ and a disciple, and in its fifth chapter the disciple suddenly breaks into something like a song. Love is a great thing, it says. It makes every heavy thing light and carries a burden without being burdened. Then a run of nothings: nothing sweeter than love, nothing stronger, nothing higher, nothing wider, nothing fuller or better, in heaven or on earth. In the Latin, nihil dulcius est amore. Why? Because love is born of God, the chapter says, and can't rest anywhere but in God. Then it shows how love moves. The lover flies, runs and rejoices. Tired, it isn't worn out. Pressed, it isn't crushed. Like a living flame, it pushes upward. And then the portrait, a list of what love is. Here's the detail to tell someone tonight: the very first word on that list is swift. Before sincere, before patient, before faithful and brave, the Imitation puts speed. Love doesn't wait until it has done the math. So the girl in the kitchen gets her answer. Patience is on the list too, and she can still respect her mom's worry. But love, here, leans toward the door.
screen: `A CONVERSATION BREAKS INTO SONG.` · `A RUN OF NOTHINGS.` · `BORN OF GOD, RESTING IN GOD.` · `THE FIRST WORD: SWIFT.` · then, large: `NOTHING SWEETER.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and think of one person who would be glad to hear from you right now. Send them one short line before you can weigh whether it's worth it. Then set the phone face down and stay with them in mind for the rest of the sit.
Nothing sweeter than love. The Imitation's song: love born of God makes the heavy light, and the first thing it is, is swift.
Your line: nothing sweeter. And on the Imitation's list, love runs before it walks. See you tomorrow.

fork.setup: your friend's dad lost his job today. you could text tonight, or wait and find the perfect thing to say this weekend. what would the Imitation's list lean toward?
options: text tonight, even a short line; love on the list is swift.

notes: Imitation III.5 paraphrased: love makes every heavy thing light, carries a burden without being burdened; nothing sweeter, stronger, higher, wider, fuller or better in heaven or on earth, because love is born of God and cannot rest but in God; the lover flies, runs and rejoices; weary it is not tired, pressed it is not straitened; like a living flame it mounts upward; love is swift, sincere, pious, pleasant, strong, patient, faithful, prudent, long-suffering, manly (virilis, rendered 'brave' after the outline) and never seeks itself. Confirm each against the Latin.
'Swift comes first' follows the Latin order ('Amor est velox, sincerus...'); confirm in the edition used.
The 1 Corinthians 13 echo is offered only as what 'some readers hear'; paraphrased, not quoted.
